{{short description|Swedish chemist}}
'''Sven-Olov Lawesson''' (9 September 1926, in [[Bräcke]], Sweden – 5 March 1985<ref>{{cite journal 
 | title = 5-Thioxoproline and 5-Thioxoproline Esters – Synthesis and Crystal Structures.
 |author1=Andersen T. P. |author2=Rasmussen P. B. |author3=Thomsen I. |author4=Lawesson S.-O. |author5=Jmgensen P. |author6=Lindhardt P. | journal = Liebigs Ann. Chem. 
 | pages = 269–279
 | year = 1986
 |doi=10.1002/jlac.198619860206 }}</ref>) was a [[Sweden|Swedish]] [[chemist]] known for his popularization of [[Lawesson's reagent]] within the chemical community.

He is also known for his 1982 work exploring the possibility of a connection between recreational use of [[amyl nitrite]] and an increased incidence of [[Kaposi's sarcoma]] in [[homosexual]] men.<ref>{{cite journal 
 | doi = 10.1056/NEJM198209303071414 
 | title = Amyl nitrite and Kaposi's sarcoma in homosexual men
 |author1=Jorgensen K. A. |author2=Lawesson S. O. | journal = New England Journal of Medicine
 | volume = 307 
 | issue = 14
 | pages = 893–4
 | year = 1982
 | pmid = 6125888
 }}</ref>

Lawesson obtained his education at [[Uppsala University]]. He did most of his work at the [[University of Aarhus]] in Denmark and his last paper was published in 1986.

After finding that 2,4-bis(4-methoxyphenyl)-1,3,2,4-dithiadiphosphetane 2,4-disulfide was useful for some reactions, Lawesson undertook a general survey of the reactivity of organic compounds with this reagent. It is often named after him as Lawesson's reagent. The synthesis of thioketones is his most cited paper.<ref>{{cite journal 
 | title = Studies on Organophosphorus Compounds .10. Synthesis of Thioketones
 | author = Pedersen B. S., Scheibye S., Nilson N, H,, Lawesson S. O.
 | journal = Bulletin des Sociétés Chimiques Belges
 | volume = 87 
 | issue = 3
 | pages = 223–228
 | year = 1978
 | doi = 10.1002/bscb.19780870310
 }}</ref>

At one point S. O. Lawesson worked with the chemist [[N. M. Yousif]]. After Lawesson's death, Yousif has been working in [[Egypt]] and has been very active within the [[phosphorus]] [[sulfur]] chemical community. Yousif has published many new [[Chemical reaction|reaction]]s of Lawesson's reagent.<ref>{{cite journal 
 | title = Applications of Lawesson's Reagent in Organic and Organometallic Syntheses
 |author1=M. Jesberger |author2=T. P. Davis |author3=L. Barner | journal = Synthesis
 | volume = 2003 
 | issue = 13
 | pages = 1929–1958
 | year = 2003
 | doi = 10.1055/s-2003-41447
 }}</ref>

Prof [[T. B. Rauchfuss]], who is in the United States did some very important work on Lawesson's reagent. He did the <sup>31</sup>P NMR experiment which proved that Lawesson's reagent could form the [[dithiophosphine]] [[ylide]]s in solution.
